messages:
lee: Quick flag: Console p95 for /v1/generate spiked after we rolled the routing-change last night. p50 stayed same, p95 and p99 diverged by ~180ms. Noticed endpoint breakdown shows two buckets but counts look off.

anika: Can you paste the endpoint breakdown? is this for region=us-west or global?

lee: region=us-west. Screenshot: https://imgur.com/a/placeholder2 . Console shows /v1/generate@backendA: p95=240ms count=4.2k; /v1/generate@backendB: p95=420ms count=210. Aggregate p95=410ms which feels wrong given proportions.

omar: That sounds like a percentile provenance problem again. If backendB has heavier tails but tiny count, naive merge can still lift aggregate p95. We should be careful how we present aggregated percentiles.

ux-claire: UX thought: users expect aggregate p95 to reflect the dominant traffic. If a tiny backend pushes aggregate upward we should highlight why (origin counts + merge policy) and offer a "dominant-weighted" toggle.

lee: Also paging rule triggered on the aggregate p95. Devops-bot: which alert fired?

devops-bot: Alert #A-334: latency-p95-rollup-exceeds-slo. Triggered at 2026-03-20T02:11:08Z. Incident opened: https://incident.redwood.ai/INC334.

anika: For immediate triage, can the alert include per-backend p95 & counts? Right now it only includes aggregate value and a sample_count. That makes it noisy.

omar: Agreed. Two parts to fix:
1) Add per-endpoint p50/p95/p99 to alert payload.
2) Decide on canonical rollup semantics: (a) compute quantile on combined samples (current), (b) weighted-by-count quantile, (c) show multivariate breakdown only.

lee: We have historical SLOs computed with (a). Can't change default silently. Suggest: keep default (a), add option (b) behind `?merge_mode=weighted` and console toggle, and include explanation in alert payload.

ux-claire: I'll prototype a small inline tooltip that says: "Aggregate p95 uses append-merge by default. Toggle to Weighted to prioritize high-volume backends." Also show a mini-sparkline per backend.

anika: Implementation detail: if we persist per-endpoint tdigest metadata (centroids + count + origin tag), we can compute weighted quantiles efficiently on read without recomputing raw samples. Storage cost minimal.

omar: Caveat: tdigest merges are not strictly reversible; computing a true weighted quantile from per-endpoint tdigests requires careful centroid merging. But we can approximate with resampling from centroids or maintain a compressed histogram for each endpoint.

lee: Which path is lower risk for rollout?

omar: Lower risk: 1) add endpoint tdigests to metrics store (no change to existing aggregate behavior), 2) implement read-path for `merge_mode=weighted` that merges per-endpoint tdigests with count weighting, 3) expose via API and console. Migration: none needed for historical data because we keep original aggregates.

anika: That sounds good. Who will own backend change?

omar: I'll pick it up. Will add `endpoint_digest` field to timeseries points and expose `/api/rollup?merge_mode=`. Will add unit tests showing a contrived case where small heavy-tail backend flips p95.

ux-claire: I'll mock the UI toggle and per-endpoint micro-charts. Also will update alert template to include per-endpoint breakdown and a short sentence: "This spike may be due to small-volume backend with high tail."

lee: Thanks. Can we add a short-run rule to suppress paging if aggregate p95 > threshold AND one endpoint count < 5% AND that endpoint p95 > 2x others? Quietly notify on slack but don't page.

anika: Sounds reasonable. Add that as an alert rule change with a feature flag for 2 weeks.

omar: Timeline: PR for schema + API by Fri, console toggle mock by Thu, alert template change + suppression rule by Friday. I'll post PR link when ready.

lee: Great. Also file a docs note: "How rolling / route merges affect percentile metrics" so on-call know what to expect.

devops-bot: Noted: DOC-TASK created (DOC-482).

lee: cool, thanks everyone. We'll reassess after the pilot. :thumbsup:
